record.notes: 59 RUB a month is the vendor's figure in the vendor's currency. The USD 0.73 in price_arithmetic is derived from the Central Bank of Russia table read on 2026-10-24 at 80.5381 RUB per USD, which is the only rate used and is not taken from memory. Whether the shared IPv4 is stable across reboots is not stated. The page says the plans are loaded from a shared catalog and match checkout; the catalog itself was not read. | 2026-10-24: this is the beefiest sub-USD-1 NAT row with UDP stated in writing - 1 GB of RAM and 999 forwarded TCP/UDP ports at USD 0.73 a month - and the cheapest 1 GB machine in the band after DediRock's annual promo. Two things hold it back: no IPv6 at all, and a payment page that lists Russian rails plus crypto with no international card and no PayPal, which makes the crypto route the only one a payer outside Russia can use. The vendor names no company anywhere on the pages read, so the counterparty question is open.

record.notes: The best port story in the band and the weakest entity story. 999 TCP and UDP ports on one shared IPv4 removes the entire problem the other NAT sellers have: no port budget, no mapping panel, no ticket, so a WireGuard listener can sit on its default port. 1 GB and 10 GB of NVMe for 59 RUB is USD 0.7257 a month at the rate read, which is 1.8 times the C-Servers monthly rate for 2.7 times the RAM. Two things hold it back. The shared IPv4 is explicitly not permanent: the offer reserves the right to reassign it at any time and tells the buyer to update their own DNS when it happens, which for a WireGuard endpoint means reissuing every peer's config. And the seller has no findable legal entity: the offer is signed '© Cheap-Host', prints no company name, no INN or OGRN and no address, and the domain was registered on 2026-06-14, four months before this reading. That is not the dissolved-company pattern - there is no company to dissolve - but it is also not an entity that can be checked, and evaluated offerings brief asks for exactly that check. Payment is the other wall: SBP, SberPay, YooMoney and MIR cards are Russian domestic rails, so a buyer outside Russia is left with cryptocurrency. Not established: the entity, whether a non-Russian buyer can pay at all, the stock of the NAT Start rung, and whether the 999 ports are reachable end to end rather than advertised.
